description: Iowa WIC provides nutrition support and eWIC food benefits through local clinics for pregnant or postpartum participants and children under five.
introduction: Iowa WIC provides nutrition support and eWIC food benefits through local clinics for pregnant or postpartum participants and children under five.

sections.who: Applicants need an Iowa address, qualifying income and a medical or nutritional need. SNAP, Medicaid or FIP participation may establish income eligibility; the clinic still completes WIC screening.
sections.get: Services include approved foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding support and health referrals.
sections.docs: Bring identity and address evidence, income records or qualifying benefit notices, and the signed WIC rights-and-responsibilities document. Ask the clinic about missing records.
sections.apply:
1. Find the local clinic through the state’s WIC location map and schedule an appointment.

  2. Complete the clinic’s eligibility and nutrition assessment. The office can supply the rights-and-responsibilities form if you forget it.
sections.after: Ask the clinic to explain the food package, eWIC shopping and follow-up appointments. Keep clinic contact information with your card instructions.
sections.sources:
Application and program details: Iowa WIC eligibility and clinic map.

Historical screenshots and background: USA Assistance. Screenshots may show an earlier application interface.

faqs: Does SNAP enrollment automatically enroll me in WIC?
No. It can establish income eligibility, but WIC requires its own clinic screening.
Contact a local WIC office and arrange an appointment.
Can the clinic supply the consent paperwork?
Yes, the office has the rights-and-responsibilities document.
It provides approved food benefits and nutrition services.
